description_full: Webull Corporation operates as a digital investment platform. The company offers various products and services, including trading, wealth management product distribution, market data and information, user community, and investor education. Its platform enables retail investors to trade securities through its licensed broker dealer in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Japan, South Africa, the Netherlands, Italy, and internationally. The company was founded in 2016 and is headquartered in Saint Petersburg, Florida.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 1K people. Revenue per employee of $409K ranks in the above the sector median among Technology peers. Each employee generates $402K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $31K per employee reflects an ownership culture.
financial_summary: Webull Corporation is a mid-cap technology business with a $2.2B market cap on $571M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +46% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +11.9pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 8% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.

The business throws off $562M in free cash flow — roughly 98 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 22.87× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 9.3×.

Net dilution runs at 7.7% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 23% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
